day_shape: 63 items: Khamenei's new armed-forces command appointments dominate regime channels, Syria-IAEA nuclear-material removal deal confirmed, reported US blockade incident in Gulf of Oman, Pakistani minister says US-Iran nearing agreement, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Khamenei armed forces appointments cascade
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and IRGC-linked channels published a wave of messages around the Supreme Leader's orders appointing new chiefs of the General Staff, IRGC and Basij, naming General Ali Abdollahi and General Ahmad Vahidi. Iran International framed the appointments as veteran commanders including a figure wanted by Interpol taking senior roles.

threads.label: Syria nuclear material removal deal
threads.summary: Syria's government confirmed coordination with the IAEA, the US and Israel to remove nuclear material from a clandestine Assad-era site, with a delegation expected in the coming days. The Jerusalem Post carried Syrian Atomic Energy Commission comments citing 'significant progress' and analyst commentary on Israeli diplomatic implications.

threads.label: US-Iran pressure, blockade and diplomacy
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported US troops fired on a Panamanian-flagged vessel in the Gulf of Oman attempting to bypass a US blockade on Iranian ports, and Pakistan's defence minister told Bloomberg the US and Iran were nearing an agreement. A separate report described a secret operation flying Trump from Turkey to the UK after an Iranian assassination threat, alongside analysis on economic pressure.

threads.label: Iranian officials on recent war
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi told Defa Press that Iran's armed forces had 'defeated the world's largest army', and an IRGC Aerospace deputy claimed Operation Honest Promise 4 rendered US missile defences ineffective despite 30 tonnes of enemy bombs. The acting defence minister told his Malaysian counterpart Iran would not 'succumb to coercion'.

threads.label: Israel operations in Lebanon and Gaza
threads.summary: Times of Israel's military correspondent reported an Israeli drone strike on a vehicle near Nabatieh with a follow-up strike hitting a Hezbollah-linked ambulance team, though the IDF later denied carrying out a Nabatieh strike. The IDF also said 99th Division troops targeted a Hamas sniper near the Gaza 'Yellow Line'.

threads.label: Regional strikes and Houthi attacks
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported two Pakistanis and an Indonesian killed in a Houthi missile strike on a commercial ship in the Bab el-Mandeb, and a rocket attack on an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp near Erbil blamed on Iran. Defa Press separately claimed Ansarullah fired ballistic missiles at the Yemeni port of Al-Mukha.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures
threads.summary: Iran International reported rising living costs pushing Iranians out of cafes, and Germany's Tehran embassy keeping visa services suspended on security grounds. Regime channels also carried warnings on tiered electricity pricing and gold-plating fraud.

events.title_en: Independent: Food price shock heading to Britain; drought has grounded farms
events.summary_en: Drought and unprecedented heat in Britain have severely reduced agricultural production, and the country's authorities have warned of a surge in food prices in coming months. Wheat, barley and oilseed harvest is expected to be around 2.5 million tonnes less than anticipated, with the effects of this shortage visible in shops over the next six to twelve months. About 71 per cent of Britain is now facing drought, and farmers are facing serious difficulties with irrigation and animal feed supply. Cheap imports from Europe cannot be a solution either, as European countries are facing severe heat.

events.title_en: Independent: Drought sweeps large part of Britain; river and reservoir water levels are falling
events.summary_en: The UK environment agency announced that nearly 71 per cent of the country's soil has entered a state of 'sudden drought', a condition that forms rapidly due to very low rainfall and intense heat. July this year was the driest July in Britain since records began in 1836, and now no area of the country is in normal conditions. Simultaneously with the fifth heat wave of the summer, river and reservoir water levels have dropped sharply and approximately 27 million people face restrictions on using water hoses. Farmers are also concerned about severe crop loss and food shortages.
